pictures.scene: Pieter Saenredam, Interior of Saint Bavo in Haarlem — the inside of a great whitewashed gothic church seen down its length, enormous round pale stone piers rising the full height of the picture and carrying tall pointed arches that open one behind another into aisle after aisle, a vault overhead ribbed in pale blue and painted all over with gold foliage scrollwork, a long chain hung with gilt beads dropping from it, tall windows of leaded glass with patches of orange and blue set high in the white walls, gilded memorial panels and small painted hatchments fixed to the piers, a brass chandelier and a carved screen at the right, worked flagstones running away across the floor, and one tiny figure in a red coat standing alone far off under the arches, in my father's house are many rooms, i am going there to prepare a place for you, …
pictures.name: pd_saenredam_interior_of_saint_bavo_haarlem

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Wanderer above the Sea of Fog — one man standing alone on the broken brown summit rocks in the middle of the picture, seen squarely from behind, his full height crossing the whole frame, in a long dark green frock coat with a white collar showing at his neck, his red gold hair blown about, one hand set on his hip and the other gripping a stick wedged among the stones, looking out over a wide sea of white mist that boils up between dark crags and buries the valley, pale blue grey ridges rising out of it one behind another, a far mountain at the left, a bare rock tower at the right, a few small pines standing on an island of rock, and a high pale sky barred with soft cloud above, you know the way to the place where i am going, lord, said thomas, we do not know where you are going, …
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_wanderer_above_the_sea_of_fog

pictures.scene: Jan Brueghel the Elder, The Sermon on the Mount — a great wooded hollow with enormous oaks and beeches standing full height across the whole upper half of the picture, their green and gold leaves spread right over the scene and one huge bough leaning in from the right, and below them a crowd of hundreds packed across the ground, Christ standing among them a little way off in a pale robe with a thin gold halo and both hands opened out as He speaks, the people nearest Him seated on the grass in blue, white and rose with their faces turned up to listen, ranks of hats, caps, turbans and white coifs filling the middle, and in the front a woman in a brilliant yellow gown sitting on the earth with a little dog beside her, a woman in scarlet with a child at her shoulder, men in black cloaks and wide hats talking in groups, and a pedlar's table of wares at the side, i am the way and the truth and the life, no one comes to the father except through me, …
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_bergrede

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, God the Father from the Ghent Altarpiece — one enormous frontal face filling the middle of the panel, grave and wide eyed and looking straight out at the viewer, a long dark brown beard parted on the breast and dark hair falling either side of the cheeks, a towering white and gold papal tiara of three jewelled crowns set with pearls, sapphires and rubies on His head, a deep crimson robe over His shoulders closed at the breast with a great round jewelled clasp of pearls and blue stones, a broad gold orphrey band sewn with pearls and little crosses hanging down either side, one hand raised at the left edge of the frame, and behind Him a burnished gold ground scored all over with fine ruled rays inside a wide gold arch cut with dark Latin letters, philip said to him, lord, show us the father, and that will be enough for us, …
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_god_the_father

pictures.scene: Konrad Witz, The Miraculous Draught of Fishes — Christ standing upright on the surface of a wide green lake in an enormous scarlet mantle that falls in heavy folds to the water, His bearded face turned in profile toward the boat and one hand opened out over the lake, His own shape doubled in the water under Him, a long wooden boat at the left with a grey bearded fisherman in a blue green robe leaning out over the side, a young man in a short white jacket hauling a bulging net full of fish up out of the water, and a third in a billowing red tunic braced at the stern with a pole, Peter below them in a dark blue coat waist deep in the lake with both hands lifted toward Him, and beyond the water a low wall of green willows, mown fields and hedges, a white chapel with a red roof, farmhouses, tiny people at work in the meadows, a green mountain rising at the right with far snow peaks behind, and a pale blue sky streaked with soft cloud, it is the father dwelling in me, performing his works, …
pictures.name: pd_witz_wonder

pictures.scene: Raphael, The Deliverance of Saint Peter — an angel standing on the prison steps in a loose apricot gold robe with the sleeves pushed back and the feet bare, wrapped from head to foot in a blaze of light that throws out fine rays on every side, one hand reaching back to beckon and the head turned down toward the guards, Peter following him out of the dark cell behind in a heavy dark robe with a thin gold halo, his grey bearded face dazed and still half asleep, a broken chain hanging from his wrist, two soldiers tumbled asleep on the stone below him in burnished steel armour and helmets with a brown cloak and a great round shield thrown down among them, a dark barred window and rough prison masonry filling the left side, and the worked grey and gold coffering of a painted arch curving down the right, he will do even greater things than these, because i am going to the father, …
pictures.name: pd_raphael_deliverance_of_saint_peter

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, An Elderly Man in Prayer — one very old man filling the whole picture, lit softly out of a warm dark brown ground, his thin grey hair swept back off a deeply lined forehead, his eyes shut and the lids heavy, a long soft white beard spreading over his breast, wearing a worn pale brown coat with a strap across the shoulder, and his two big knotted hands pressed flat together in front of him and held up at his chin, the knuckles and worn fingers catching the light, and below them on the table the pages of a great open book lying open with the lines of print just showing, if you ask me for anything in my name, i will do it, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_elderly_man_in_prayer

pictures.scene: El Greco, Pentecost — a white dove hanging in a blaze of gold light at the very top of a tall dark vault, long grey rays breaking down from it, and under the vault a close standing press of twenty or more figures with a little pointed tongue of flame burning over every head, Mary in the middle in a deep blue mantle over a rose crimson robe with both hands put together at her breast and her face lifted straight up into the light, a man at the left throwing one bare arm up above his head in a blue sleeve, an old man in a brilliant yellow mantle beside her with his hands opened out, a green cloaked apostle and a white veiled woman crowding in at the right, grey bearded faces tipped back on every side with their mouths open, and in the front others in green, crimson, gold and blue seen from behind with their arms flung out, he will give you another advocate to be with you forever, the spirit of truth, …
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_pentecost

pictures.scene: David Adolf Constant Artz, The Sewing Room of the Orphanage at Katwijk — a plain whitewashed room with heavy dark beams overhead, a tall carved oak cupboard along the left wall with two blue and white Delft bowls standing on top of it, and a leaded window at the right with a painted coat of arms in the glass letting a shaft of daylight in across the floor, an old woman in spectacles seated behind a bare deal table in a black jacket and a white cap with a long white kerchief crossed at her breast, her head bent over a piece of white linen she is stitching, a young orphan girl seated at the left in a black dress, a white cap and a long grey blue apron with her needle in her hand and her eyes down on her work, another girl standing between them with her hands folded and her head bowed, a stack of folded linen, spools, scissors and a red pincushion laid out on the table, a turned oak stool in front and the scrubbed plank floor running away below, i will not leave you as orphans, i will come to you, …
pictures.name: pd_artz_weeshuis

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Noli Me Tangere — the risen Christ standing at the right of a walled garden in a long white robe that falls in soft folds to His bare feet, a slender hoe over His shoulder, a flat gold halo marked with a red cross behind His fair hair and short beard, His face bent down and one hand lowered toward the woman kneeling before Him, Mary Magdalene down on the grass at the left in a pale rose gown with a wide orange gold mantle fallen about her, her long gold hair loose on her shoulders and a gold halo round her head, both arms stretched out toward Him and her face lifted to His, a dark green meadow between them starred all over with small white and red flowers, a tall palm and dark trees rising behind, a woven wattle fence running right across the garden, and a pale painted band closing the fresco at the left edge, i will love him and reveal myself to him, …
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_noli_me_tangere

lines.text: Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God; believe in Me as well. In My Father's house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you?
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.
You know the way to the place where I am going.
Lord, said Thomas, we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?
Jesus answered, I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
If you had known Me, you would know My Father as well. From now on you do know Him and have seen Him.
Philip said to Him, Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.
Jesus replied, Philip, I have been with you all this time, and still you do not know Me? Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, Show us the Father?
Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in Me, performing His works.
Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me, or at least believe on account of the works themselves.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in Me will also do the works that I am doing. He will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.
And I will do whatever you ask in My name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you ask Me for anything in My name, I will do it.
If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever,
the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.
I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.
In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me. Because I live, you also will live.
On that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you are in Me, and I am in you.
Whoever has My commandments and keeps them is the one who loves Me. The one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.
Judas not Iscariot asked Him, Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?
Jesus replied, If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word. My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.
Whoever does not love Me does not keep My words. The word that you hear is not My own, but it is from the Father who sent Me.
All this I have spoken to you while I am still with you.
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.
Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled; do not be afraid.
You heard Me say, I am going away, and I am coming back to you. If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it does happen, you will believe.
I will not speak with you much longer, for the prince of this world is coming, and he has no claim on Me.
But I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me, so that the world may know that I love the Father. Get up! Let us go on from here.
